To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the neurotrophic/immunotrophic effects of astroglia cells on LHRH neuronal cells are mediated by a complex array of signaling molecules including growth factors and cytokines; (ii) LHRH neurons and astroglia are interconnected by a complex array and variety of signaling molecules, including growth factors, adhesion and intercellular communication molecules, and hormones; (iii) the LHRH neuronal-astroglia interactions are mediated by a variety of inter
astroglial cells play a major role during the development and in the functional regulation of LHRH neurons.

(1) astrocytes can modulate LHRH neuronal development, differentiation and function, both "in vivo" and "in vitro"; (2) astroglia and neuronal cells can communicate with each other via growth factor(s), neurotransmitters and adhesion molecule(s); (3) the neuronal and astrocyte compartments interact via a complex network of signaling molecules, including cytokines and nitric oxide; (4) astroglia-derived growth factors can regulate LHRH neuron development
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the role of neurotrophins, hormones, adhesion molecules, and intercellular signals in the CNS and, in particular, with the role of these molecules in neuron-astroglial interactive networks, with particular reference to the LHRH neuronal-glial network.

the study of the mechanisms of action of neurotrophic factors on LHRH neuronal development, and the role of these factors as mediators of the interactions between LHRH cells and glial cells in the hypothalamus.
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms involved in the control of the LHRH system
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neuroendocrine function is the result of a complex network of interactions involving a variety of neuronal and non-neuronal cells.
astroglial cells are not simply a "supporting" tissue but a major contributor in the control of neuronal function.

the astroglia-LHRH neuronal network represents a model of a functional neuro-glial unit, in which the glial cells are able to modulate the neuronal phenotype and function through a variety of soluble factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LHRH neuron-glia network, through a complex interplay of growth factors, adhesion proteins and other intercellular signaling molecules, is involved in the regulation of the reproductive axis.
LHRH neuron-glia interactions may play a crucial role in the regulation of reproductive function.
LHRH neuron-glial interactions are mediated by a complex network of growth factors and other informational molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the astrocytic compartment is a major source of neurotrophic factors and cytokines, and that these molecules are involved in the regulation of LHRH secretion, proliferation and differentiation.
astrocytes can be a source of growth factors that are essential for the differentiation and maintenance of the LHRH neuronal system.
astroglia cells are not only passive bystanders but rather play an active role in the regulation of LHRH neuroendocrine function.
